notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, as reported to the MA Division of Local Services on Schedule A, not a budget.

Includes public schools. Massachusetts cities and towns pay for their schools and their share of any regional school district through the town budget, where most other states have separate school districts, so spending and property tax per resident run higher than in those states.

Covers the general fund, special revenue funds (federal and state grants, school lunch, revolving and other special revenue), capital projects and enterprise funds such as water and sewer: $1,550,629 of revenue and $1,582,811 of spending outside the general fund. Trust funds, transfers between funds and borrowing are left out. Fire, water and other districts inside the town are separate governments and are not included.
Debt is all long-term debt the town reported outstanding at the end of FY 2025 (Schedule A Part 10), including school construction and any water, sewer or other enterprise fund borrowing.
"Taxes" on Schedule A include motor vehicle and other local excises ($272,569), which are shown as other local taxes. The rest, with penalties and interest, is shown as property tax.

Fixed costs ($808,225: health insurance, pensions and other benefits for town and school staff) are spread across departments in proportion to their size, schools included, as with benefits in other states. Debt service is left out of that spread.
Intergovernmental assessments and other spending ($60,825: charter school tuition, regional transit and county and state charges) are spread across departments in proportion to their size.
Political money is not scored: no party committee or candidate for this town files with the Office of Campaign and Political Finance, and candidates for town office file with the town clerk.
